subject: penguin
reasoning:
I'm planning a stylized low-poly penguin built from primitives, standing upright facing forward at roughly 0.6-0.7m tall, with a scaled sphere for the dark body, a flattened white belly shape, and separate pieces for the head and other features.

Working out placement...

Now I'm working out the head placement as a slightly flattened sphere sitting atop the body, then positioning the eyes as small white spheres with black pupils, and adding orange-yellow cheek patches as flattened ellipsoids on either side of the face.

For the beak, I'm using a cone rotated 90° about the X-axis so its tip points forward along +Z, positioning it centered on the face so the base meets the head surface and the tip protrudes slightly in front.

Now I'm setting up feet as flattened boxes positioned under the body, colored orange, and starting on the flippers—using scaled spheres as ellipsoids placed on each side of the body with a slight outward rotation so they hang naturally with the bottom edge angled away from the torso.

Next I'll shape the tail using a cone tilted backward and slightly upward near the base of the body, working out the rotation angle so the tip points back and up convincingly.

For materials I'm setting up shared colors: dark body black, white belly, orange beak and feet, yellow cheeks, and reusing the black for the eye pupils. I'm making sure the feet sit flush on the ground and the body bottom aligns just above it, then considering a subtle gradient on the belly for extra visual polish.
